name: Path of Ancestry
oracle_text:
This land enters tapped.
{T}: Add one mana of any color in your commander's color identity. When that mana is spent to cast a creature spell that shares a creature type with your commander, scry 1. (Look at the top card of your library. You may put that card on the bottom.)
blocked_sentences: {T}: Add one mana of any color in your commander's color identity. When that mana is spent to cast a creature spell that shares a creature type with your commander, scry 1. (Look at the top card of your library. You may put that card on the bottom.)

needs.what: an `add_mana` form whose colour options are the union of the colour identities of the activating player's commanders, resolved when the ability is activated rather than baked at load -- e.g. `{"op": "add_mana", "any_color_of": "commander_color_identity"}`, offering exactly those colours (and nothing at all, the ability being unactivatable, for a colourless commander). `Player.commanders` already holds the oids and `CardDef.color_identity` is already a `frozenset[str]`, so the data exists; what does not is a path from a mana ability to it. `cards/loader.py:_mana_options`/`_sum_mana` bake a fixed tuple of 6-tuples at load, and `engine/costs.py` (`mana_options`/`offerable_mana_ability`) plus the mode chips built in `engine/legality.py` and the castability solver in `engine/mana.py` (`ManaSource.options`/`producible`) all read that constant, so every one of them has to consult a resolver taking `GameState` and the activating player instead.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `add_mana` takes a literal `mana` string parsed once at load, and the only sanctioned way to offer a choice -- a single `choose_mode` of `add_mana`s, which `_sum_mana` restricts mana abilities to -- has its mode list written into the card. That is exactly what the packet's `starting_point` does, and it is wrong rather than incomplete: five fixed modes is Command Tower in a five-colour deck and a strictly better card in every deck narrower than that, letting the land pay for spells the printed card cannot pay for. There is no way to prune the modes either -- a mana ability may contain only `add_mana`, so `if` and every `condition_keys` entry is rejected inside one, and `_validate_mana_amount` additionally forbids amounts depending on X, targets, bindings or a loop because a mana ability is activated mid-payment. Nothing in `selector_keys` or `value_keys` reads a commander's colour identity: `is_commander` selects the commander as an *object* and `colors` reads a permanent's current colour, which is not the same set (colour identity includes mana symbols in rules text and is read off the card in the command zone, which may not be on the battlefield at all). This shares its engine work with the `reflecting_mana` gap (Exotic Orchard) -- both need a mana ability's option set to become a function of GameState -- but the source of truth is different (the command zone, not the battlefield), so it is a distinct card group: Command Tower, Arcane Signet, Commander's Sphere and Opal Palace all want this one.

needs.what: provenance on produced mana, plus a trigger that fires when a specific unit of mana is spent: a mana ability must be able to tag the mana it makes with its source and a rider, and the payment path must fire a `mana_spent` event carrying the spell that was cast and the tag, so "When that mana is spent to cast <filtered spell>, <effect>" can be authored as a trigger on the land itself. Concretely, `ManaPool.amounts` (a flat `list[int]` of six counts) has to gain a parallel record of tagged pips, `ManaPool.spend`/`assign_hybrid` must decide which tagged pips were consumed and report them, and `stack.py`'s cast path must emit the event after the spell is on the stack. The Path of Ancestry / Opal Palace shape also needs the tag to survive being carried across the whole payment of one spell rather than being consumed per-pip.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The pool has no provenance whatsoever: `ManaPool` stores six integers, so once the land's mana is added it is indistinguishable from any other mana of that colour and "that mana" cannot be identified at spend time. The nearest existing feature is `ManaSource.restriction` (the loader's `mana_restriction`, "spend this only to cast a creature spell"), and its own docstring says it is deliberately implemented by *filtering sources before the solver sees them* rather than by tagging the pool -- it gates what may be paid, and never reports what was paid, so it cannot carry a rider. `delay` is the other shape of after-the-fact effect but `DelayedTrigger.step` is matched against `DELAY_STEPS` in engine/turn.py, i.e. a turn step, so it can say "at the beginning of the next end step" and cannot say "when this mana is spent". `spell_cast` fires for every spell regardless of what paid for it, so hanging the scry there would trigger on creature spells cast entirely off other lands -- a different, strictly better card. And none of it can live in this ability anyway: `_sum_mana` rejects any effect that is not `add_mana`, and dropping `is_mana_ability` to smuggle the trigger in would stop the land being tappable during cost payment, which is the only reason it is played.

needs.what: let a filter compare a card's creature types against the controller's commander's creature types without an effect-time binding -- e.g. `{"shares_a_type_with": "your_commander"}`, or a `shares_a_type_with` that accepts a selector rather than a binding name, so "a creature spell that shares a creature type with your commander" can be spelled on a trigger filter
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `shares_a_type_with` in engine/effects/selectors.py resolves its argument through `_bound_oid(ctx, name)`, i.e. it names an object bound earlier in the same effect by a target or a trigger -- and returns False when nothing is bound. There is no binding for "your commander", and the commander is usually not the object this trigger is about, so there is nothing to bind. `is_commander` is a *predicate on the object being tested* ("is this permanent a commander"), not a reference to compare a different object against, and it is a battlefield-object test while the commander here may be in the command zone. A literal subtype list cannot stand in either: the relevant creature type is a property of whatever deck the card is played in, not of Path of Ancestry.

notes: The first printed line, "This land enters tapped.", is already fully expressible and is covered by the packet's `replacements` entry -- only the mana ability's line is blocked. That line is blocked twice over and the two halves are independently useful: `commander_color_identity` alone unblocks Command Tower, Arcane Signet and Commander's Sphere, while `mana_spent_trigger` is the smaller group (Path of Ancestry, Opal Palace) and is the harder engine change.
